resources.string: Your phone. Your code.\nNo laptop in the loop.
Open Termux once first. Allow commands below, follow the one-time connection instructions, then install OpenCode.
Open your workspace and start a conversation.
This stops this server’s running AI tasks and terminals, then closes OpenCode Mobile. Chats and files are kept. Other Termux sessions and apps are left alone.
OpenCode is off. Tap Launch OpenCode to start it again.
Copy the command, paste it in Termux, and press Enter. Return here and tap Check Termux connection. This allows apps you authorize to run Termux commands.
This runtime requires Android 10 or newer, a 64-bit ARM phone, and 64-bit ARM Termux. This device does not report ARM64 support.

Everything runs on this phone. Termux does the work; this app is the screen.
Use Termux from F-Droid or its official GitHub releases. Open it once before setup. Install OpenCode adds a third-party OpenCode 2 build and trusts its package repository (bd-loser/opencode-bionic). 

Projects start in ~/projects inside Termux. For shared phone folders, run “termux-setup-storage” there once. 

Requires Android 10 or newer and 64-bit ARM Termux. Keep Android System WebView updated. Internet is needed for installation and online AI providers. 

Termux keeps the server running through its own notification. Android may still stop it. Use the power icon to stop this app’s server without affecting other Termux sessions. Back returns here.
